# Module Objectives

At the end of this module, you should be able to:

- prepare date variables with `lubridate`;
- summarize delays by group while accounting for the number of observations;
- visualize relationships between numerical or categorical variables;
- calculate and interpret a simple correlation;
- formulate exploratory conclusions without overclaiming.

# Setup

The exercises use the `flights_merged_2023.rds` file.

```r
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)

flights <- readRDS("flights_merged_2023.rds")
```

# Consolidation Exercises

## Exercise 1 - Check the Structure

Load the data, display the structure and verify the number of rows and columns.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### Answer

```r
glimpse(flights)

flights |>
  summarise(
    n_flights = n(),
    n_columns = ncol(flights)
  )
```
:::

## Exercise 2 - Create Temporal Variables

Create the `date`, `weekday` and `moment_day` variables.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### Answer

```r
flights <- flights |>
  mutate(
    date = make_date(year, month, day),
    weekday = wday(date, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE),
    moment_day = case_when(
      hour < 6 ~ "night",
      hour < 12 ~ "morning",
      hour < 18 ~ "afternoon",
      TRUE ~ "evening"
    )
  )

flights |>
  select(date, weekday, hour, moment_day) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)
```
:::

## Exercise 3 - Identify Important Missing Values

Calculate the number of missing values in `dep_time`, `dep_delay`, `plane_year`, `wind_gust`, `visib` and `precip`.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### Answer

```r
flights |>
  summarise(
    dep_time_missing = sum(is.na(dep_time)),
    dep_delay_missing = sum(is.na(dep_delay)),
    plane_year_missing = sum(is.na(plane_year)),
    wind_gust_missing = sum(is.na(wind_gust)),
    visib_missing = sum(is.na(visib)),
    precip_missing = sum(is.na(precip))
  )
```
:::

## Exercise 4 - Mean Delay by Hour

Calculate the mean departure delay by scheduled departure hour. Also include the number of flights by hour.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### Answer

```r
hourly_delays <- flights |>
  group_by(hour) |>
  summarise(
    n_flights = n(),
    mean_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

hourly_delays |>
  arrange(desc(mean_delay))
```
:::

## Exercise 5 - Visualize Delays by Time Slot

Produce a boxplot of `dep_delay` by `moment_day`. To keep the graph readable, limit the display to delays between -30 and 180 minutes.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### Answer

```r
flights |>
  filter(!is.na(dep_delay), between(dep_delay, -30, 180)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = moment_day, y = dep_delay)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of delays by time of day",
    x = "Time of day",
    y = "Departure delay (minutes)"
  )
```
:::

## Exercise 6 - Weather Correlation

Calculate the correlation between `dep_delay`, `wind_gust`, `visib` and `precip`.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### Answer

```r
flights |>
  select(dep_delay, wind_gust, visib, precip) |>
  cor(use = "complete.obs") |>
  round(2)
```

A weak correlation does not prove that a variable is useless. It only indicates that the global linear relationship is weak in this summary.
:::

## Exercise 7 - Weather Scatterplot

Create a scatterplot between `wind_gust` and `dep_delay`. Use a sample of 5,000 flights to keep the graph readable.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### Answer

```r
flights |>
  filter(!is.na(wind_gust), !is.na(dep_delay)) |>
  slice_sample(n = 5000) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = wind_gust, y = dep_delay)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Wind gusts and departure delays",
    x = "Wind gusts (mph)",
    y = "Departure delay (minutes)"
  )
```
:::

## Exercise 8 - Plane Age

Create `plane_age`, group flights into age bands and calculate mean delay and cancellation rate.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### Answer

```r
flights |>
  mutate(
    plane_age = 2023 - plane_year,
    age_group = cut(
      plane_age,
      breaks = c(-Inf, 5, 10, 15, 20, Inf),
      labels = c("0-5", "6-10", "11-15", "16-20", "21+")
    )
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(age_group)) |>
  group_by(age_group) |>
  summarise(
    n_flights = n(),
    mean_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE),
    cancellation_rate = mean(is.na(dep_time)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```
:::

## Exercise 9 - Compare Airlines

Identify the ten airlines with the most flights, then compare their mean delay.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### Answer

```r
top_airlines <- flights |>
  count(name, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10)

flights |>
  semi_join(top_airlines, by = "name") |>
  group_by(name) |>
  summarise(
    n_flights = n(),
    mean_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_delay))
```
:::

## Exercise 10 - Write a Cautious Conclusion

Choose one result from the previous exercises and write two sentences:

1. one sentence that describes the observed result;
2. one sentence that states a limitation or an alternative explanation.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
### Example Answer

If mean delays appear higher in the evening, you could write:

> Flights scheduled in the evening show higher mean delays in these data. This comparison remains descriptive because it does not control for destination, airline, weather or delay accumulation throughout the day.
:::
